UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

Plaintiff,  v.  KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6,

Defendants. ____________________________________/

Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

PLAINTIFF’S RULE 54(b) MOTION TO RECONSIDER ECF NO. 108 AS TO ECF NO. 105

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine moves under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 54(b) for reconsideration of the Order signed and filed October 29, 2026 and entered October 30, 2026 (ECF No. 108), insofar as it denied Plaintiff’s Motion for an Order Directing Completion of the Rule 26(f) Conference and Submission of a Discovery Plan (ECF No. 105). ECF No. 108 also denied Plaintiff’s separate motion for a scheduling order (ECF No. 103). This Motion does not seek reconsideration of that disposition. This Motion is addressed to the Magistrate Judge who entered ECF No. 108. It asks him to revise his own interlocutory order within the authority referred under 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)(1)(A). It is not an objection under Rule 72(a). Under Local Civil Rule 7(F), a supporting memorandum, Proposed Order A, and Proposed Order B accompany this Motion.

I.	GROUNDS

1.	ECF No. 105 requested a conference and one report. ECF No. 105 requested an order directing Plaintiff and counsel for each appearing Defendant to complete the conference Rule 26(f) requires by a date certain and to file one written report stating the parties’ agreed proposals and each party’s separately attributed position on the subjects Rule 26(f)(3) requires the discovery plan to address. ECF No. 105 ¶ 11(a)–(c). The report would record any party’s proposal to postpone, phase, or limit discovery. ECF No. 105 ¶¶ 6, 11(b). ECF No. 105 asked that, if the Court postponed the conference, the order identify the scope of the postponement and a definite date or event for renewed consideration. ECF No. 105 ¶ 12.

2.	ECF No. 105 excluded discovery responses and modification of ECF No. 84. ECF No. 105 requested no answers to interrogatories, no production of documents, no sanctions, and no modification of ECF No. 84. ECF No. 105 ¶ 8. It did not renew the requests that ECF No. 84 denied. Id. It asked the Court to decide when the conference would occur, and it left every proposal concerning the sequencing or postponement of substantive discovery to the report. ECF No. 106 at 5.

3.	ECF No. 108 denied the planning request on the attributed discovery-postponement decision. ECF No. 108 identified the request as one for “an order directing the parties to complete a Rule 26(f) conference and file respective discovery plans.” ECF No. 108 at 1. Its case-specific ground is stated in one sentence: “Here, the record reflects that the District Judge has chosen to refrain from beginning any discovery until resolution of the pending motions to dismiss.” ECF No. 108 at 2. It denied ECF No. 105 without prejudice. Id. ECF No. 108 may reasonably be read as postponing the parties’ conference and report until the pending motions to dismiss are decided. It does not state whether initial disclosures are postponed. It does not state what step follows the dismissal rulings. Plaintiff asks the Court to reconsider the application of the discovery-postponement decision to the planning request and to state the operative scope of any postponement that remains.

4.	Planning can proceed under an order that does not impose or extend a discovery stay. Rule 26(d)(1) places the conference before discovery. Rule 26(a)(1)(C) runs initial disclosures from the conference “unless a different time is set by stipulation or court order.” Rule 26(d)(2)(B) treats a document request delivered early as served at the first Rule 26(f) conference, and Rule 34(b)(2)(A) provides that a different response time may “be ordered by the court.” The Court’s authority under Rules 16 and 26 over the timing and sequence of discovery permits it to determine that timing and sequence after considering the report. Proposed Order A does not independently impose or extend a discovery stay. The timing of substantive discovery, initial disclosures, and responses to requests delivered under Rule 26(d)(2) remains governed by the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and any applicable stipulation or express court order. Any party requesting postponement, phasing, or modification of discovery or disclosure obligations may state that position and its grounds in the report for judicial determination. A conference and report on those terms require preparation and participation. Proposed Order A does not itself order discovery responses, document production, depositions, or initial disclosures.

5.	The reconsideration ground. Plaintiff invokes the ground of clear error causing manifest injustice. Carlson v. Boston Sci. Corp., 856 F.3d 320, 325 (4th Cir. 2017). Plaintiff asserts no new evidence and no change in law. The asserted error is that ECF No. 108 applied a ground directed to the commencement of discovery to a request that sought no discovery and that itself supplied the vehicle for each Defendant’s proposal to postpone discovery. The asserted consequence is that court-directed planning is deferred for the full pendency of the motions to dismiss, without terms stating what is postponed, whether disclosures are postponed, or what step follows the dismissal rulings. When Plaintiff executed the declaration accompanying ECF No. 105, the parties had not completed the conference and no report existed. ECF No. 107 ¶¶ 10–11.

6.	The alternatives. If the Court declines to find error in the original disposition, Plaintiff asks the Court to consider the narrowed terms in Proposed Order A as a renewed request. ECF No. 108 denied ECF No. 105 without prejudice. Plaintiff does not contend that the characterization of the request as renewed exempts it from the principles that govern reconsideration. If the Court determines that planning remains postponed, Plaintiff requests Proposed Order B, which states the scope of the postponement, identifies the direction on which it rests to the extent the Court relies on one, and establishes the procedure that follows disposition of the pending motions to dismiss.

II.	SCOPE

7.	This Motion does not seek reconsideration of the disposition of ECF No. 103. It does not seek reconsideration of ECF No. 84. It does not renew ECF No. 15 or ECF No. 54. It does not ask the Court to adopt Plaintiff’s discovery proposals, to impose sanctions, or to find that any party acted in bad faith. It does not ask the Court to adjudicate any dismissal or immunity defense. It does not seek relief concerning the designation of the Magistrate Judge. Plaintiff’s pending objections and applications remain presented on their own grounds, and this Motion withdraws and replaces none of them.

III.	LOCAL CIVIL RULE 37(E)

8.	This Motion seeks reconsideration of a case-management ruling. It does not seek an order compelling a disclosure or a response to a discovery request. Local Civil Rule 37(E) reaches motions concerning discovery matters, and Plaintiff does not contend that this Motion is categorically outside that rule. ECF No. 105 § III disclosed Plaintiff’s written efforts to obtain the appearing Defendants’ participation and disclosed that no telephone or in-person consultation concerning that request had occurred. Those efforts appear in ECF No. 107 and Exhibits A through C-2. Plaintiff does not represent that the correspondence satisfies Local Civil Rule 37(E). If the Court determines that Local Civil Rule 37(E) applies to this Motion, Plaintiff requests permission to proceed on the existing record or, in the alternative, an opportunity to complete the consultation the Court requires before the Motion is decided on that ground.

IV.	RELIEF REQUESTED

9.	Plaintiff requests that the Court grant reconsideration of ECF No. 108 insofar as it denied ECF No. 105 and enter Proposed Order A, which:

(a)	modifies ECF No. 108 as to ECF No. 105 only and leaves its disposition of ECF No. 103 unchanged;

(b)	directs Plaintiff and counsel for each appearing Defendant to complete the Rule 26(f) conference within 14 days after entry, by substantive written exchange on the subjects in Rule 26(f)(2)–(3) or by another format the participants agree on or the Court directs;

(c)	directs the parties to file the written report within 14 days after completing the conference and no later than 18 days after entry, stating the parties’ agreed proposals and each party’s separately attributed position on each subject in Rule 26(f)(3), including any proposal to postpone, phase, or limit discovery;

(d)	provides that, if the conference remains incomplete at the reporting deadline, the parties shall file a status report, that a party unable to obtain a joint report shall file its own, and that a status report does not complete the conference, extend the completion deadline, or excuse further participation;

(e)	provides that the order does not independently impose or extend a discovery stay; that the timing of substantive discovery, initial disclosures, and responses to requests delivered under Rule 26(d)(2) remains governed by the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and any applicable stipulation or express court order; that any party requesting postponement, phasing, or modification of discovery or disclosure obligations may state that position and its grounds in the report for judicial determination; that nothing in the order decides whether ECF No. 108 independently imposed a discovery stay or modifies any other applicable order; and that the Court may determine the timing and sequence of discovery and disclosures after consideration of the report; and

(f)	leaves existing preservation duties, the disposition of ECF No. 103, and all pending motions, objections, and applications unchanged.

10.	In the alternative, if the Court determines that planning must remain postponed, Plaintiff requests that the Court enter Proposed Order B, which:

(a)	states that the parties’ Rule 26(f) conference and report are postponed pending disposition of the motions to dismiss at ECF Nos. 10, 21, and 45, and states the corresponding treatment of initial disclosures and discovery;

(b)	states the source and scope of any direction of the District Judge on which the postponement rests, to the extent the Court relies on one, or states that the postponement rests on this Court’s own determination under Rule 26(f)(1);

(c)	directs Plaintiff and counsel for the parties remaining in the action to file a status report within 14 days after disposition of the last of those motions, unless a final judgment has ended the action, identifying the remaining claims and parties, any leave to amend and its deadline, proposed dates for the conference, the report, and initial disclosures, and any continuing request for postponement;

(d)	permits any party to request earlier planning as to claims that remain pending after a ruling on fewer than all of those motions; and

(e)	leaves existing preservation duties and all other dispositions and pending applications unchanged.

11.	The 14-day period to complete the conference and the 18-day outer limit for the report are requested terms. The 14-day period to file the report after completing the conference tracks Rule 26(f)(2).

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court enter Proposed Order A or, in the alternative, Proposed Order B.

Marvelle J. Ballentine
